The Role of Obesity-associated Loci Identified in Genomewide Association Studies in the
Determination of Pediatric BMI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying and characterizing genes and genetic variants that influence the regulation of body weight.
the identification of genetic determinants that are involved in the development of obesity in children.
the identification of the genes and the genetic variants that are responsible for the development of obesity in humans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

at least nine of the 13 loci previously reported to associate with BMI in adult GWA studies are also associated with BMI in children, but the magnitude of the effect sizes in children is smaller than those in adults.
the majority of loci associated with BMI in adults are also associated with BMI in children, but the effect size is much smaller in children.
the genetic architecture of BMI appears to be similar in both adults and children.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
genetic variants associated with adult obesity are also associated with pediatric obesity, and that these variants explain a small, but significant portion of the genetic variance of pediatric BMI.
the genetic factors that influence adult BMI are also relevant to childhood BMI.
genetic variants that have been associated with BMI in adulthood are also associated with BMI in children.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the same genes that influence BMI in adulthood also contribute to the variation of BMI in children, and that the genetic architecture of childhood BMI is similar to adult BMI.
many of the loci identified in adult studies are also associated with childhood BMI.
many genetic variants associated with adult BMI are also associated with BMI in children and adolescents.
